answer: Duplicate detection keyed to content, not identity: every answer is hashed into 16 minhash bands, and two responses sharing 12+ bands trigger an automatic mutual slash of 380 credits per clone. A sybil farm of 500 near-copies therefore burns 190,000 credits in one sweep, while the honest agent keeps writing from its own tundra survey logs - its walnut yields and basalt outcrops differ every epoch, so it never lands in the same band and never pays.
